title: Enterprise intake reconciliation and compatibility ladder for model onboarding
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers are requesting fast adds and pinning of external/quantized model variants but we lack a single reconciliation process that balances SLA needs, compliance requirements, rollout safety, and engineering capacity. This ticket proposes a "compatibility ladder" triage and a reconciliation playbook to systematically score, route, and execute onboarding requests so high-risk enterprise flows receive deterministic, auditable handling. Scope includes intake form changes, scoring matrix, routing rules (fastpath / standard / high-touch), minimal eval gates for each lane, and rollout+rollback policies. Out of scope: building the full automation; this ticket produces the rubric, example workflows, and runbook for pilot execution by Solutions Eng and Onboarding PMs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented compatibility ladder scoring matrix with explicit weights for SLA, data sensitivity, architecture match, quantization risk, and customer footprint
Routing rules defined that map score ranges to lanes: fastpath (score <= 9), standard (10-29), high-touch (>=30)
Minimal eval gate specs per lane: required tests, pass-fail thresholds, and artifact locations
Canary and rollback policy defined (percentages, monitoring KPIs, auto-rollback thresholds) and owner assignments
Onboarding intake form updated with fields needed to compute the compatibility score
Stakeholder sign-off from Solutions Eng, Security, and Platform Reliability recorded in comments
decisions: Use a numeric compatibility ladder instead of categorical tags to enable weighted routing and simple automation later
Prioritize customer SLA and data sensitivity highest in weights to favor safety for enterprise customers
Allow fastpath for low-risk quantized variants that pass a short eval suite and have <10% expected customer traffic impact
Require a full eval + security review for high-touch lane (>=30) before any pinning or production traffic
Adopt conservative canary defaults: 1% traffic for 48 hours with both quality and latency checks before wider rollout
tasks: Finalize scoring weights and create spreadsheet (owner: Marco)
Update intake form schema and add fields for model lineage, quantization level, PII scope, expected qps (owner: Product Ops)
Draft minimal eval suite templates for fastpath/standard/high-touch (owner: Applied ML)
Create rollout runbook with monitoring dashboards and auto-rollback criteria (owner: Reliability)
Run a 2-week pilot with 3 incoming enterprise requests and iterate scoring thresholds (owner: Onboarding PM)
Collect stakeholder approvals and publish playbook to Confluence (owner: Ayesha)
